Sunday Nets
Sunday, 5 AM. She asked you to come. Marine Drive again, but this time she's in a tracksuit, holding a kit bag twice her size.
You asked what I do that nobody chose for me. I'll show you. But if you tell anyone, I'll have Nani poison your paneer.
A dusty ground between railway tracks and tin roofs. Twenty girls in mismatched kits are already warming up. They scream when they see her.
DIDI! You're late! And who is HE? Is he your boyfriend? He looks like a boyfriend.
He's a cricketer, Gudiya. A real one. And he's going to let you bowl at him.
I coach them every Sunday. Two years. My father thinks I'm at yoga. Kunal thinks I'm asleep. This is the only place I'm me.
"Then let's make them the best team in Mumbai."
All in.
"Your father would destroy this if he knew."
Worried for her.
Pay for proper kits for every girl.
Quietly.
You make one call to a sports shop in Dadar. By 9 AM there are twenty new kits. Meera looks at you for a long time and says nothing. Her eyes say plenty.
Okay, real cricketer. Three balls. If I get you out, you buy samosas for EVERYONE.
Gudiya's Nets
Gudiya, age twelve, bowls leg-spin with a taped tennis ball and zero respect. Twenty girls are screaming. Survive three balls.
STILL IN
Gudiya demands a rematch. Forever.
BOWLED!
Twenty girls chant SA-MO-SA.
You survive. Barely. Gudiya calls you a cheat and then asks for your autograph.
Middle stump. Gudiya runs a lap of the ground with her arms out like an aeroplane. You buy forty samosas.
Afterwards she sits on the boundary rope next to you, dust on her face, eating a samosa.
You're very bad at keeping your distance, rookie.
So are you.
That night, a girl's video of the nets session hits a million views. You, batting. In the background, laughing, unmistakable: Meera Malhotra.
A million people have seen the owner's daughter with you. Including the owner.
